rationale:
Evidence from iteration 4 (score 870.2, best so far). The oval (20/20, rms 0.005) and s-bend (20/20, rms 0.011) both finish comfortably. The slalom is the only failure: 13/20 finish, 7 end off track, mean progress 0.90, and about 0.4 line-loss events per run. No slalom run timed out, so the robot is fast enough. The problem is tracking at direction reversals, not speed. Lighter body and narrower track (iteration 4) raised slalom progress from 0.74 to 0.90, which confirms that lower yaw inertia and more steering authority help. The slalom still has steering_oscillation 0.27 and control_effort 12.9, which points to a proportional gain that is too low to hold the tape through fast reversals.

Change: kp 4.5 -> 5.0, with everything else held at iteration 4 values (geometry, base_speed 0.95, kd 2.5, ki 0, line_loss last_direction). This is a single-variable test. A higher kp gives more correction per unit of sensor error at each reversal, and kd 2.5 should still damp it.

Expected result: slalom off-track exits fall from 7 toward 3 or fewer, and slalom mean score rises above about 800. The oval should stay near 950, provided steering_oscillation there remains below about 0.3.

Hypotheses to check next: (1) If oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.35 or s-bend rms rises above 0.013, kp 5 is too aggressive and should go back to about 4.75. (2) If the slalom still leaves at similar progress (about 0.9), the limit is sensor coverage at the +/-0.04 m edges, so the next step is seven sensors at about 0.0133 m spacing across +/-0.04 m, not a wider spread. (3) If line_loss_events on the slalom stay near 0.4, the line is lost on sharp reversals, and a search direction or a lower base_speed through reversals should be tested. Measurements requested: all metrics per track, so slalom finish count, off-track versus finished split, and steering_oscillation can be compared directly with iteration 4.
